key_insight: This paper argues that multi-turn fashion search should not assume every user interaction is just an attribute edit. It introduces a benchmark and approach aimed at handling diverse intent changes while preserving fine-grained visual details.
problem_solved: Existing multi-turn fashion image retrieval methods oversimplify user behavior by treating all interactions as the same kind of attribute-editing process. They also often convert multimodal queries into text, which can discard important visual cues needed for accurate retrieval.
method: Introduces DIM-Fashion, a benchmark designed to capture heterogeneous intent transitions in interactive fashion retrieval.
Moves beyond single-paradigm attribute editing to support diverse multi-turn user intents across interactions.
Reduces reliance on textification so the retrieval system can better preserve and use visual details from fashion images.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides a more realistic benchmark for evaluating interactive retrieval systems in fashion e-commerce and similar settings. It also highlights a path toward better multimodal retrieval models that maintain visual precision across conversation turns.
visual_elements: A before/after diagram showing traditional attribute-editing turns versus diverse intent transitions

paper_authors: Mingqiang Tang, Haokun Wen, Meng Liu, Yupeng Hu, Weili Guan
